I used Windsurf (Cascade chat inside the editor) to complete the coding portion of HW08 Q2: SSM Forward Passes across the CPU and GPU notebooks. In my setup, Windsurf was running Claude Opus 4.5 as the underlying LLM. 

The task was to implement the SSM recurrence

h_t+1​=W h_t​+U x_t ​ + b

both as an unrolled recurrence and via a convolution-based method (including the diagonal optimization), and then validate correctness + discuss runtime behavior. 

Overview of Performance

Windsurf delivered 100% correct code for the assignment’s coding tasks. The convolution and recurrent implementations matched numerically via sanity checks (max absolute differences on the order of ~1e-8), and the GPU/diagonal optimizations were implemented consistently with the notebook’s expectations.

Outcomes

One-shot success rate (code): 100%
 All coding subproblems were completed correctly without needing iterative debugging.

High Success

Algorithm → PyTorch translation: Correctly converted the SSM math into working PyTorch for both CPU and GPU paths.

Shape & layout discipline: Handled Conv1d layout and causal alignment correctly, backed by strong numerical agreement in sanity checks.

Diagonal optimization: Correctly leveraged diagonal structure for efficiency while preserving correctness. 

Limitations (non-code)

Verbosity: The assistant sometimes produced more explanation than necessary, which can slow review even when the final code is right.

Agent UI verification: As with most agent interfaces, I still manually ran the notebooks to confirm everything (sanity checks, timings, outputs). 

Hallucinations

None that affected correctness. The main “risk” was extra verbosity, not wrong implementations.

Bottom line: For HW08’s SSM forward-pass coding, Windsurf + Claude Opus 4.5 was fast and highly reliable—able to implement the full solution correctly in one pass.
